awards.title: Hack the North 2025 - (1) Finalist (Highest award), (2) Best Developer Tool by Warp
awards.description: Winning Hack the North Finalist and Best Developer Tool from Warp, Puppeteer unlocks runtime understanding for developers. By probing live variables and simulating traffic on the fly, it removes backend blockers and accelerates frontend development with AI.

awards.title: CuHacking 6 - (1) Best Use of Gemini API, (2) Best Marketing Challenge
awards.description: Winning Best Use of Gemini API and Marketing Challenge, FocusBuddy is an AI-powered platform that generates personalized short-form videos to enhance focus. Using the Gemini API for content creation and OpenCV for attention tracking, it detects when users lose focus and nudges them back with visual and audio cues. Built with React, Flask, and TailwindCSS, it blends entertainment and productivity.

li_projects.title: HealthBase
li_projects.description: Our product HealthBase, allows medical professionals to have their own login and connect it to their organization. From there, the individual can either input new patient data or access existing patient data available in the database. Thus, allowing it to be easily transferred across medical teams as a replacement for the inefficient faxing system. Event: Steel City Hacks: Winter Hack

li_projects.title: Autonomous Mars Rover
li_projects.description: This product detects the distance from the car to the nearest potential collision. When the tracker determines the distance to be at risk of a collision or bump, it will bring the vehicle to a stop. From there, the vehicle will be able to manipulate its direction in order to continue in a safe path. Event: Hack the North

posts.text: Happy to be heading back to RBC this summer as a Software Developer Co-op, joining the Wealth Management Technology team! Big thanks to Daisy Asare-Akoto for making the process smooth, and to Priyanka Paliwal, CSM®, CSPO® for her support early on. Excited to dive back in and keep building!

From Hacker to Co-Director: Building Ottawa’s Largest Hackathon This past weekend, uOttaHack 8 truly came alive. Having first participated in uOttaHack three years ago, it has been a meaningful part of my early university years, connecting me to people and the hackathon community across the country. This year, I had the honour of serving as Co-Director of uOttaHack 8. After months of planning, finally seeing hundreds of hackers building, learning, and collaborating in the same space was incredib

🚀 Propelling Ideas to Impact: Building the platform behind Canadian innovation Over the past four months, I contributed to NRC IRAP’s digital platform that enables Canadian startups and SMEs to access funding, advisory services, and innovation support. I’m very grateful to KW Goldwyn-Pearson and my co-op peer, Mohammed Abdulla, for their guidance and support throughout the term. Beyond my co-op role, the fall term included a few other highlights: 🏆 Hack the North Finalist + Best Developer Tool (

💜 From hacker to mentor at Hack Western. One year, full circle. Last year, I was a hacker at this exhilarating event, walking away with memories to last. This weekend I got to come back as a mentor. I helped teams bounce around ideas, turn early visions into real projects, and perfect their pitches. Watching hackers unblock tough problems and ship meaningful work in 36 hours was truly inspiring. Shoutout to the mentors: Mouiz Majid, Jimmy Liu, Jasleen Bakshi, Oscar Yu, Hugo N., Isabelle Gan, HAM
